validity.recommendation: Escalate to Baird: this row is a genuine, real historical project (not a hallucination) but it is a CRUDE OIL pipeline proposal, not gas. It is the precursor entity to the operating Double E GAS pipeline (P0061, swept in slice 1) -- a 2011 joint venture ('Double E Crude Pipeline LLC', Energy Transfer Partners + Enterprise Products Partners) to move crude from Cushing, OK to Gulf Coast refineries, which collapsed in 2011 when Enterprise pulled out; the pipe was never built. In 2018 an unrelated/successor entity re-proposed a much smaller GAS project under the same 'Double E' name (135 mi, NM->TX Permian gas takeaway, now operating as P0061), which is where P5727 (Red Hills Lateral) belongs. Fuel=Oil is factually correct for THIS row's project, but a Fuel=Oil row's place in the GAS tracker is a scope question, not a data-quality one -- Baird should decide whether GGIT keeps it as project genealogy/history on the gas system, or whether it should be dropped from GGIT entirely (oil precursor entities are GOIT's territory, which is out of scope this cycle -- not researching or staging anything there).
validity.researcher_notes: NOT a duplicate of P5727. P5727 'Double E Red Hills Lateral' (Poker Lake Metering Station -> New Mexico, 20 mi, 24-in, 600 MMcf/d, proposed) is a real expansion lateral of the CURRENT, operating natural-gas Double E system (P0061, the 2018 re-proposal, swept in slice 1) -- a completely different physical pipeline in a completely different era, commodity and geography from P7830. P7830's own worklist values (SegmentName='Original Proposal (Oil Pipeline)', Fuel='Oil', CancelledYear='2011') already flag it as the pre-2018 entity, and two independent, dated, named sources confirm this directly: Dallas Business Journal (2011-09-30, via Wayback) states ETP 'formed a joint venture in April [2011] with Enterprise called Double E Crude Pipeline LLC to build an oil pipeline from Cushing, Okla., to the Gulf Coast', and that Enterprise 'sen[t] out a news release ... saying the Double E joint venture was terminated' in 2011 before ETP sued. Dallas Morning News (2014-03-04) independently confirms the same 2011 'Double E' JV between Energy Transfer Partners and Enterprise Products Partners to 'construct a crude oil pipeline from Cushing, Okla., to the Gulf Coast.' Both are independent news organizations (not one wire story reprinted), both name the 'Double E' project explicitly, and both agree: real project, oil commodity, 2011 collapse, never built. I read gem.wiki's own intro prose for leads only (never cited): it frames P7830 and P0061 as the same article's two eras ('initially proposed as an oil pipeline but cancelled in 2011 ... in 2018 the project was re-proposed, with new owners and a reduced length and capacity, to carry gas instead of oil'), which matches what I independently verified. cross_row_leads below names P0061 as the row this precursor's history belongs to; P5727 is unrelated to P7830 and stays untouched.

validity.recommendation: Correct StartState/Province to Oklahoma (Cushing) now -- both independent sources name it directly. EndState/Province ('New Mexico' as currently recorded) is also established wrong (this project never touched New Mexico) but I could not confirm the specific end state: both sources say only 'the Gulf Coast', not a named state. Cushing-to-Gulf-Coast crude lines of that era typically terminated in the Houston/Texas Gulf Coast refining complex, so Texas is the likely candidate, but I would not stage it as sourced without a source naming it -- flagging for a follow-up read of the original 2011 Energy Transfer/Enterprise press release ('Cushing to Houston Crude Oil Pipeline Capacity', per its title as harvested in gem.wiki's own citation list -- I could not independently fetch it: governance.energytransfer.com 403s curl with a browser UA and no Wayback capture exists for that exact URL after repeated attempts).
